vulnerability_mechanism.evidence: CVE-2025-49178 is PUBLISHED, and the 2025-06-17 X.Org advisory describes the same cross-client denial-of-service mechanism seen in os/io.c: a completed request may leave ConnectionInput.ignoreBytes nonzero, yet the input buffer is made AvailableInput and later recycled for another client, whose request is then ignored.

atomic_bic.evidence: Bounded history search through xorg-server-1.10.0 finds cf88363db0ebb42df7cc286b85d30d7898aea840 as the first -S ignoreBytes commit. Its two-file patch adds the field, oversized-BigReq assignment, ignore path, and the gotnow=0 state immediately before the pre-existing AvailableInput publication; later c80c41767eb101e9dbd8393d8cca7764b4e248a4 only repairs long-read accounting.

immediate_parent_absence.evidence: The sole parent is fa22f97af65efc2a147e9be0b7f288848965ff60. git grep finds no ignoreBytes in its os tree, and its oversized-request path calls YieldControlDeath() and returns -1 while retaining the older unguarded AvailableInput path; the vulnerable state interaction is absent.

squash_member_decomposition.evidence: cf88363db0ebb42df7cc286b85d30d7898aea840 is a normal one-parent public commit with a focused 25-insertion/3-deletion patch in os/io.c and os/osdep.h, not a merge, move, revert, or squash aggregate; no finer public member decomposition is applicable.

affected_fixed_release_membership.evidence: The BIC is not an ancestor of xorg-server-1.9.5 but is an ancestor of xorg-server-1.9.99.901 and xorg-server-1.10.0, matching X.Org's 'Introduced in: Xorg 1.10.0'. Patch-equivalent fix commits are absent from xorg-server-21.1.16 and xwayland-24.1.6, and present in xorg-server-21.1.17 and xwayland-24.1.7, matching the official fixed-release boundary.

direct_fix_or_unpatched.evidence: Canonical direct fix d55c54cecb5e83eaa2d56bed5cc4461f9ba318c2 changes only `if (!gotnow)` to `if (!gotnow && !oci->ignoreBytes)` in ReadRequestFromClient; its parent ab02fb96b1c701c3bb47617d965522c34befa6af is still vulnerable. Release cherry-picks 7996ac60d81d665a87f4f736bcfe17e22a375b5c and 41ae2e70ade30ff8d1447fcb465d666c16cd8dc3 name the canonical commit and all three patches have stable patch-id 4d873d97950521d4fe5859f1e5f03d5c31e16c59.

bic_only_ai_attribution.evidence: AI attribution was evaluated only on cf88363db0ebb42df7cc286b85d30d7898aea840. The 2010 commit object names Aaron Plattner as author and Keith Packard as committer, contains only Signed-off-by and Reviewed-by trailers, and has no AI/copilot/bot/co-author marker; its 2010 provenance predates modern generative coding assistants. The 2025 fix was not used to attribute the BIC.

findings: The primary vulnerability mechanism, atomic BIC, parent, and direct-fix claims reproduce from the assigned clone.
Official advisory state and introduced/fixed release claims reproduce against CVE/X.Org records and local tag ancestry.
No correction to the primary NOT_AI verdict or structured provenance fields is required.
